summary: New sense 2: jmndm. eine Wohltat vergelten, jmndn. belohnen

data.gloss: jmndm. eine Wohltat vergelten, jmndn. belohnen

rationale: A king offering his whole city cannot repay the addressee's benefit; 1sg kəmkafe- with recipient -nux differs from continuing and from III makfe suffice. One attestation; homonym placement remains provisional.

data.turoyo: U mede, d obenux, u mede d samno, obenux, i walayayḏi kula, lo kəmkafenux u mede, d səmlux ṭowuṯo ʕam.
data.translation: Wenn ich dir etwas gebe, was ich auch tue, wenn ich dir meine ganze Stadt gebe, so entgelte ich dir damit doch nicht das gute, das du an dieser Stadt getan hast.

rationale: Single clear repayment use; gift, recipient and benefit are explicit. Filing under II is provisional, with no invented etymology.

summary: The meaning is grounded in the Turoyo sequence obenux ... walayayḏi kula ... lo kəmkafenux ... ṭowuṯo: giving even the city fails to recompense the addressee's benefit.
Read-only lookups distinguish kfy 1 stülpen and kfy 3 III makfele/makfe genügen from the II mkafe base here. Existing kfy 2 II.1 fortfahren and its single example remain unchanged.
The 1sg finite subject is the giver/king and -nux indexes the rewarded person; the benefit is also expressed as a noun phrase with relative clause.
Arabic kāfaʔa is only a comparison raised by the reader, not an established etymology. The inherited unknown etymology remains; no new root, stem or unattested base form is asserted.
The supplied evidence gives one lexical use, not a fixed light verb collocation.
Does kəmkafenux belong with kfy 2 II, or to a distinct recompense loan/homonym possibly comparable to Arabic kāfaʔa? The meaning is clear but homonym filing needs confirmation.
